display.title: Episode 167: The Mystery of Toras Emes, Chapter 2
display.summary_short: The Mystery of Toras Emes concludes: a dream warns the rabbi about the empty Torah scroll just in time. Plus the Shema and a listener family's letter from Connecticut.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens with a lively march for drum and drumsticks, then recaps chapter one: the jealous officer tricked Chaim the shammes into preparing an empty, make-believe Sefer Torah for the rabbi to carry when greeting the king. A young member of Tzivos Hashem who loves learning the Twelve Pesukim by heart leads the Shema. The story continues as the town prepares a royal welcome and the officer tells the king that the Jews are fooling him, so the king agrees to look inside the scroll, warning the officer that a false accusation will cost him dearly. The night before, the rabbi dreams three times of a voice calling 'Toras emes, a true Torah'. He goes to the shul, discovers the empty scroll and replaces it with a real Sefer Torah. As with Haman, the plot turns against its maker: the officer is punished and the king gives the Jews even more freedom. Uncle Yossi explains 'bayamim hahem bizman hazeh': in the merit of children learning Torah and doing mitzvos, Hashem protects us today too and will bring Moshiach. After a sponsor message, Uncle Yossi dives into the mailbox for a letter from a family in Connecticut whose uncle rebroadcasts the show to twelve states.
display.lesson: In the merit of Jewish children learning Torah and doing mitzvos, Hashem protects His people and turns their enemies' plots against them, then and now.
